newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary forint up vs dlr, unmoved by devaluator.
newsitem.headline: Hungary forint up vs dlr, unmoved by devaluator.

text.p: Hungary's forint firmed against the dollar on the mark's overnight gains on Wednesday, dealers said.
The trading volume was average and the market was unaffected by Tuesday's announcement about a cut in the monthly crawling peg devaluator to one percent from 1.1 percent on August 15, dealers said.
"(The decision) absolutely did not have any impact on the turnover," said Jozsef Laczi of ING Bank. "Perhaps it needs a little time to react."
The forint opened at 185.00/05 to the dollar and, tracking the dollar/mark, edged up to 185.14/18 by 0841 GMT, compared with Tuesday's close of 185.34/39.

The decision on the devaluation rate cut could not strengthen the forint further versus the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) currency basket as the forint have traded right at the NBH resistance level for weeks, dealers said.
They said the devaluator cut widened the difference between forint and foreign currency interest rates and that may boost both futures and spot currency trading, but the market's were slow to react.
"The (currency futures) market has to digest (the rate cut)," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Tozsdeugynoki Rt. "(The rate cut) is likely to boost the interest of investors."
